# Cow (Mario)
Cow (Mario), known in Japanese as Ushi (ウシ) and often referred to as Moo Moos, is a species of cattle in the Mario video game franchise. These cow characters resemble real-world dairy cows and typically appear as placid farm animals roaming on all fours. They were first introduced as background fauna in the 1996 game Mario Kart 64 and have recurred as obstacles on farm-themed race courses (such as Moo Moo Farm and Moo Moo Meadows) in the Mario Kart series. In 2025, a cow was included as a playable racer for the first time in Mario Kart World, leading to unexpected popularity in the fan community and widespread media attention. The character’s design – which includes a brass nose ring – also prompted controversy, as the animal rights group PETA publicly urged Nintendo to remove the ring due to its real-world cruelty connotations.
## Appearances in the Mario series
In the Mario Kart games, cows (or “Moo Moos”) are most commonly associated with rural track environments. In Mario Kart 64 (1996) they appear in the background of the Moo Moo Farm course, marking their first appearance in the franchise. Later titles gave the cows a more active role: for example, Mario Kart Wii (2008) introduced the course Moo Moo Meadows, where several cows wander onto the track as moving obstacles. Players must steer clear of these cows, as colliding with one will cause a racer to crash or spin out. Cows reappear in Mario Kart 8 (2014) and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, which not only brought back Moo Moo Meadows (featuring cows of varying colors) but also incorporated the cow motif into trackside details – such as advertisements for “Moo Moo Meadows Milk” and sponsor logos displaying cartoon cow images. Beyond the core racing titles, the Mario Kart Tour mobile game includes cow-themed customization (like a Moo Moo Mii Racing Suit) as a nod to these creatures, and the mixed-reality Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit (2020) features Moo Moos as obstacles on its Windmill Meadows track.
Outside of Mario Kart, cows have made brief cameo appearances in various Mario spin-offs. In the party game Mario Party 2 (1999), for instance, a herd of cattle is visible in the background of the Western Land board’s scenery. The pinball-themed Mario Pinball Land (2004) includes a hidden bonus event in which hitting a Monty Mole may cause a Moo Moo to pop out of a hole; if Mario strikes the cow before it disappears, he earns extra points. Cows also feature in Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games, appearing as part of the obstacles on the Moo Moo Meadows equestrian course in a dream event. These recurring cameos underscore that the Moo Moos are a recognizable element of the Mario universe’s rural settings, even when they are not central to gameplay.
## Playable character in Mario Kart World
Mario Kart World, released for the Nintendo Switch 2 in 2025, marked the first time a cow was made a playable character in the Mario franchise. In this game, one of the selectable racers on the roster is simply called Cow – an anthropomorphic version of the familiar Moo Moo that drives a vehicle. The Cow character retains the look of a black-and-white dairy cow (complete with a neck bell and nose ring) but is able to ride motorbikes and karts alongside traditional Mario characters. According to the game’s art director, Masaaki Ishikawa, the idea to promote the cow from a background obstacle to a full racer originated from an informal sketch made during development. The development team was designing a ranch-themed course and brainstorming new racers when “one of the designers came up with that silly sketch of Cow cruising along,” Ishikawa recalled, and it unexpectedly fit well with the game’s lighthearted style. Encouraged by this concept, the team quickly prototyped the Cow as a racer and found she did not feel out of place. This creative decision also led them to consider other non-traditional characters: the final game’s roster additionally introduced a Cheep Cheep (a fish enemy) and a Pokey (a cactus creature) as playable racers, both of which, like the Cow, had previously only been obstacles or background creatures in Mario games. The Cow racer in Mario Kart World is categorized as a heavy-weight character (similar in performance to characters like Donkey Kong or Wario), reflecting her large size.
## Reception and controversy
The inclusion of Cow as a playable racer in Mario Kart World was met with an enthusiastic response from players. Upon the game’s launch, many fans immediately gravitated toward the humorous idea of racing as a cow. Reports noted that online multiplayer lobbies were quickly dominated by players choosing Cow, to the point that entire races of human competitors playing as the cow were commonly observed. Social media platforms saw a surge of memes and gameplay clips celebrating the bovine driver – for example, viral videos showed the Cow character dancing or lip-syncing to songs like “Mooo!” by Doja Cat and “La Vaca” by Mala Fe, garnering millions of views. The New York Times described Cow as Mario Kart World’s “breakout star,” noting that the once-minor background animal had unexpectedly become a centerpiece of the game’s popularity. Nintendo’s producers admitted they had underestimated how popular the cow would become; Mario Kart World producer Kosuke Yabuki remarked that the company was surprised by the character’s fanbase but was pleased by the positive reception.
While most of the fan reaction was lighthearted, the Cow character did spur some debates and an external controversy. Within the community, players jokingly speculated about the fact that the Cow’s in-game animations show her eating a hamburger – some fans half-seriously dubbed her a “cannibal cow” for seemingly enjoying beef, whereas others argued it might be a meat-free veggie burger, reflecting tongue-in-cheek lore for the character. Nintendo representatives declined to comment on these humorous theories. A more serious criticism came from People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA), which took issue with the Cow’s design. In August 2025, PETA sent an open letter to Nintendo urging that the brass ring be removed from the cow’s nose. The organization argued that nose rings are instruments of animal control and cruelty in real-life farming, and that depicting a family-friendly character with such a device “glosses over real-world violence and cruelty to animals”. PETA asked Nintendo to let the character “race freely – without any painful reminders” of exploitation. The plea – which even punned that Nintendo should “leave the rings to Sonic” (a reference to Sega’s ring-collecting Sonic games) – drew media attention, though Nintendo did not publicly respond. As of the end of 2025, the Cow remains in Mario Kart World with her nose ring intact, continuing to charm players as an offbeat addition to the Mario cast.

Model from _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ |
| **First appearance** | _[Mario Kart 64](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_64 "Mario Kart 64")_ ([1996](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_games_by_date#1996 "List of games by date")) |
| **Latest appearance** | _[Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_Party_Jamboree_%E2%80%93_Nintendo_Switch_2_Edition_%2B_Jamboree_TV "Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV")_ ([2025](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_games_by_date#2025 "List of games by date")) |

**Cows** (also referred to as **Moo Moos**)[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMoo-1)[\[2\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMooTwo-2) appear as a recurring species in the [_Super Mario_ franchise](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(franchise/) "Super Mario (franchise)"), first appearing in _[Mario Kart 64](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_64 "Mario Kart 64")_. They are primarily associated with farm-based courses in the _[Mario Kart](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart "Mario Kart")_ series, in which they typically act as obstacles.

History\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")\]
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### _Mario Kart_ series\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mario Kart series")\]

#### _Mario Kart 64_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mario Kart 64")\]

[![Image 2: Moo Moo Farm from Mario Kart 64.](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/e/e3/Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png/200px-Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png)

Cows can be seen in the background of the _Mario Kart 64_ course [Moo Moo Farm](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Farm "Moo Moo Farm").

#### _Mario Kart: Double Dash!!_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Mario Kart: Double Dash!!")\]

Although cows themselves do not appear in _[Mario Kart: Double Dash!!](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart:_Double_Dash!! "Mario Kart: Double Dash!!")_, [Mushroom City](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mushroom_City "Mushroom City") has a truck advertising the Moo Moo Farm course with the image of a cow.

#### _Mario Kart DS_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Mario Kart DS")\]

In _[Mario Kart DS](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_DS "Mario Kart DS")_, cows once again appear in the background of [N64 Moo Moo Farm](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Farm "Moo Moo Farm"). It is the first game to give them the blue collars with hanging golden bells.

#### _Mario Kart Wii_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Mario Kart Wii")\]

[![Image 3: A cow in MKW](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/6/60/MushroomCow.png/140px-MushroomCow.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MushroomCow.png)

A Moo Moo as seen in _Mario Kart Wii_

In _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_, cows serve as obstacles in the course [Moo Moo Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows "Moo Moo Meadows"). When hit, they cause the player to spin out. While the ones seen up close use full models, some in the distant background reuse flat textures from _Mario Kart DS_. A truck in the [Moonview Highway](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moonview_Highway "Moonview Highway") course also has a picture of a cow printed on it with the text "[Moo Moo Dairy](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_brands_debuting_in_Mario_Kart_Wii#Moo_Moo_Dairy "List of brands debuting in Mario Kart Wii")".

#### _Mario Kart 7_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Mario Kart 7")\]

Two cows make a small appearance in _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_ on a sign in the [Wii Coconut Mall](https://www.mariowiki.com/Coconut_Mall "Coconut Mall") course, which reads "Moo Moo Dairy".

#### _Mario Kart 8_ / _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Mario Kart 8 / Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")\]

Moo Moos return in _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ with the return of the Moo Moo Meadows track, with some Moo Moos now having other colors, such as solid black or brown. Also, in [Toad Harbor](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad_Harbor "Toad Harbor") and the game's rendition of [Toad's Turnpike](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad%27s_Turnpike "Toad's Turnpike"), there are advertising trucks and signs with Moo Moos on them. There is also a sponsor known as [Moo Moo Meadows Milk](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_brands_debuting_in_Mario_Kart_8_and_Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe#Moo_Moo_Meadows_Milk "List of brands debuting in Mario Kart 8 and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe"). In this game, Moo Moos appear in four different colors; white with blue spots, white with brown spots, black, or brown. The Mii Racing Suit based on a Moo Moo appears in the _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe_%E2%80%93_Booster_Course_Pass "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass")_.

#### _Mario Kart Tour_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Mario Kart Tour")\]

[![Image 4: The Moo Moo Mii Racing Suit from Mario Kart Tour](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/c/c0/MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png/60px-MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png)

Although Moo Moos themselves do not appear in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_, the Moo Moo Meadows Milk sponsor returns in several courses in the game, and the [Moo Moo Mii Racing Suit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mii "Mii") and [Moo Moo Offroader](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Offroader "Moo Moo Offroader") are both based on them and were introduced in the [Animal Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Animal_Tour "Animal Tour").

#### _Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")\]

In _[Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Live:_Home_Circuit "Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")_, the [Windmill Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Windmill_Meadows "Windmill Meadows") features some Moo Moos as obstacles.

#### _Mario Kart World_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Mario Kart World")\]

[![Image 5: Cow in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/3/37/MKWMooMoo.jpg/200px-MKWMooMoo.jpg)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWMooMoo.jpg)

Cow racing in _Mario Kart World_.

In _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World "Mario Kart World")_, cows return as obstacles on Moo Moo Meadows. In addition, a cow appears as a playable character for the first time in the _[Super Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(franchise/) "Super Mario (franchise)")_ franchise as a whole. Her [emblem](https://www.mariowiki.com/Emblem "Emblem") consists of a stylized depiction of her face. Moo Moo Meadows also now features a large golden statue of a cow on a bike.

The playable cow is unlockable in version 1.0.0, but made available from the start following a software update. She is a heavyweight character, sharing statistics with [Wario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wario "Wario"), [Waluigi](https://www.mariowiki.com/Waluigi "Waluigi"), [Donkey Kong](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong "Donkey Kong"), [Wiggler](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wiggler "Wiggler"), [Chargin' Chuck](https://www.mariowiki.com/Chargin%27_Chuck "Chargin' Chuck"), and [Pianta](https://www.mariowiki.com/Pianta "Pianta").

Missions

Cows are featured in the following [missions](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Mario_Kart_World_missions "List of Mario Kart World missions") in _Mario Kart World_:

| Mission | Location | Time limit (seconds) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [![Image 6: Mario Kart World P-Switch Mission "Moove through the herd of cows!"](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/f/f8/Mario_Kart_World_P_Switch_Missions_Moove.png/200px-Mario_Kart_World_P_Switch_Missions_Moove.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:Mario_Kart_World_P_Switch_Missions_Moove.png)  
_Mooove through the herd of cows!_ | [Moo Moo Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows "Moo Moo Meadows") | 15.00 | The player must maneuver through a large crowd of cows and reach the goal ring in time. |

### _Mario Party_ series\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Mario Party series")\]

Moo Moos make four background appearances in the [_Mario Party_ series](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party_/(series/) "Mario Party (series)"). They appear in the background of [Western Land](https://www.mariowiki.com/Western_Land "Western Land") in _[Mario Party 2](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party_2 "Mario Party 2")_ and _[Super Mario Party Jamboree](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_Party_Jamboree "Super Mario Party Jamboree")_ and [Fowl Play](https://www.mariowiki.com/Fowl_Play "Fowl Play") in _[Mario Party 3](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party_3 "Mario Party 3")_, and in _[Mario Party: Island Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party:_Island_Tour "Mario Party: Island Tour")_, they appear on [Perilous Palace Path](https://www.mariowiki.com/Perilous_Palace_Path "Perilous Palace Path").

### _Mario Pinball Land_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Mario Pinball Land")\]

In _[Mario Pinball Land](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Pinball_Land "Mario Pinball Land")_, there is a rare chance for a Moo Moo to pop out of a hole by hitting a [Monty Mole](https://www.mariowiki.com/Monty_Mole "Monty Mole"). If [Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario "Mario") hits the Moo Moo before it disappears, he gains 100,000 [points](https://www.mariowiki.com/Point "Point").

### _Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games")\]

Cows reappear in _[Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_%26_Sonic_at_the_London_2012_Olympic_Games_/(Wii/) "Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games (Wii)")_ on Moo Moo Meadows as obstacles in the [Dream Equestrian](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dream_Equestrian "Dream Equestrian") event.

### _Yoshi_ series\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Yoshi series")\]

#### _Yoshi's Woolly World_ / _Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Yoshi's Woolly World / Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World")\]

Although Moo Moos themselves do not appear in _[Yoshi's Woolly World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Yoshi%27s_Woolly_World "Yoshi's Woolly World")_ and _[Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Poochy_%26_Yoshi%27s_Woolly_World "Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World")_, Moo Moo Yoshi is available as an unlockable Yoshi [pattern](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Yoshi_designs_in_Yoshi%27s_Woolly_World "List of Yoshi designs in Yoshi's Woolly World") which resembles a Moo Moo.

#### _Yoshi's Crafted World_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Yoshi's Crafted World")\]

In _[Yoshi's Crafted World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Yoshi%27s_Crafted_World "Yoshi's Crafted World")_, the Moo Moo Meadows Milk sponsor from _Mario Kart 8_ makes various cameo appearances on the cartons and signs in the background of the flip side of [Rail-Yard Run](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rail-Yard_Run "Rail-Yard Run") and [Go-Go Yoshi](https://www.mariowiki.com/Go-Go_Yoshi "Go-Go Yoshi"). As first seen on the front side of Rail-Yard Run, there are also five cardboard Cow [crafts](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_crafts_in_Yoshi%27s_Crafted_World "List of crafts in Yoshi's Crafted World"), which serve as [Coal Blockafeller](https://www.mariowiki.com/Blockafeller "Blockafeller")'s first souvenir request. There is additionally a Cow [costume](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_costumes_in_Yoshi%27s_Crafted_World "List of costumes in Yoshi's Crafted World") for Yoshi to wear.

### Other appearances\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Other appearances")\]

#### _Nintendo Badge Arcade_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Nintendo Badge Arcade")\]

Cows[\[3\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-badge-3) appear as badges in _[Nintendo Badge Arcade](https://www.mariowiki.com/Nintendo_Badge_Arcade "Nintendo Badge Arcade")_ that the player may collect and decorate their Nintendo 3DS HOME Menu with. They are a part of the _Mario Kart 8_ set of badges.

#### _Minecraft_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Minecraft")\]

In the Super Mario Mash-Up Pack in _[Minecraft](https://www.mariowiki.com/Minecraft "Minecraft")_, the traditional [Cow](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Cow "minecraftwiki:Cow")'s design is replaced with the Moo Moo design found in the _[Super Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(franchise/) "Super Mario (franchise)")_ titles. Red and green Moo Moos with mushrooms on their back replace Mooshrooms.

Naming\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Naming")\]
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The name "Cow" (capitalized as such) is used in-game in _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World "Mario Kart World")_. Prior to this, supplementary material variously referred to them as "cows" (in lowercase)[\[4\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-switch-4)[\[5\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-7)[\[3\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-badge-3) or "Moo Moos"[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMoo-1)[\[2\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMooTwo-2) (alternatively lowercased as "moo moos"),[\[4\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-switch-4) with the latter being primarily used by third-party guidebooks. Though the name "Moo Moo" has never been explicitly used to refer to them in-game, it is implied in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ by the name of the Moo Moo [Mii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mii "Mii") Racing Suit.

Everyone Keeps Picking Cow In Mario Kart World, Of Course
=========================================================

Cow is the early breakout character for Mario Kart World, and that's the udder truth.

By [Blair Marnell](https://www.gamespot.com/profile/blairmarnell/) on June 6, 2025 at 9:59AM PDT

[1 Comments](https://www.gamespot.com/articles/everyone-keeps-picking-cow-in-mario-kart-world-of-course/1100-6532182/#comments-block-33635915)

Where to buy

[Mario Kart World](https://www.gamespot.com/games/mario-kart-world/)

There are currently no available deals

GameSpot may get a commission from retail offers.

  

Cows or Moo Moos have been a part of the Mario Kart franchise since 1996's Mario Kart 64. However, [Mario Kart World](https://www.gamespot.com/articles/mario-kart-world-isnt-titled-mario-kart-9-because-nintendo-wants-to-take-the-series-to-the-next-level/1100-6531709/)\--one of the launch titles for [Switch 2](https://www.gamespot.com/gallery/best-nintendo-switch-2-games/2900-6618/)\--is the first game in the series to feature a cow behind the wheel. And fans seem to love playing as Cow online.

Images and videos of players picking Cow have been shared all over social media (via [Polygon](https://www.polygon.com/nintendo-switch-2/604129/mario-kart-world-cow-meme?taid=6841c615d752a100010a4204)) since Mario Kart World debuted earlier this week.

> 新作マリオカート、ウシ大人気でマジ草[#マリオカートワールド](https://twitter.com/hashtag/%E3%83%9E%E3%83%AA%E3%82%AA%E3%82%AB%E3%83%BC%E3%83%88%E3%83%AF%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB%E3%83%89?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/My1dGFS0UU](https://t.co/My1dGFS0UU)
> 
> — マメソラ (@mamesora14) [June 5, 2025](https://twitter.com/mamesora14/status/1930645086465040631?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

> God, never in my whole life that I had lot of fun with Mario Kart World 🫶🏻 10/10 for me. Also, COW MAINS RISE UP MOOO 🐄 [pic.twitter.com/GRynbFwpKI](https://t.co/GRynbFwpKI)
> 
> — Ryan (@Clawspls1) [June 5, 2025](https://twitter.com/Clawspls1/status/1930766472357220540?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

> Anyone else’s online lobbies look like this in Mario Kart World? I’ve been in 3 full cow races [https://t.co/3EW1KwuYjh](https://t.co/3EW1KwuYjh)
> 
> — PhillyBeatzU | BeatzGames (@PhillyBeatzU) [June 5, 2025](https://twitter.com/PhillyBeatzU/status/1930775494116438512?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

> The first guy to post a montage of the Moo Moo Meadows Cow winning races in Mario Kart World Tour to the song La Vaca by Mala fe, Is getting the Latino pass at the Carne Asada [pic.twitter.com/kqd2chdfVc](https://t.co/kqd2chdfVc)
> 
> — Vance (@vancedotexe) [June 6, 2025](https://twitter.com/vancedotexe/status/1930975980065362144?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

In retrospect, this shouldn't be too surprising. There was an inordinate amount of interest in Cow after she was first spotted in the Mario Kart World teaser. Art director Masaaki Ishikawa subsequently revealed that the decision to turn Cow into a playable character [came from a silly drawing](https://www.gamespot.com/articles/how-a-silly-sketch-led-to-cow-becoming-a-pivotal-character-in-mario-kart-world/1100-6531712/) one of his colleagues made while working on the game.

The Cow can [eat burgers in MKW](https://www.gamespot.com/articles/mario-kart-worlds-cow-can-eat-burgers-and-steak/1100-6530642/), and she even hilariously seems to love it. That's led some to call her a cannibal, while others suggest that she's been eating a vegetarian meat substitute rather than consuming her own kind. Both of those theories may be overthinking the character a little bit.

Producer Kosuke Yabuki has acknowledged that Nintendo completely [underestimated Cow's popularity](https://www.gamespot.com/articles/mario-kart-worlds-cow-is-a-bigger-hit-than-nintendo-imagined-may-not-be-a-cannibal/1100-6532020/), but the company is happy with her reception. He also declined to weigh in about the cannibal or vegetarian theories.

Mario Kart World is out now on Switch 2, and you can keep picking Cow as long as you want to.

![Image 2](https://cdn.geekwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartcow.png)

Cow, a breakout star in the new “Mario Kart World” video game, wears a nose ring that is viewed as a painful accessory by the animal rights group PETA. (Screenshot via Nintendo on YouTube)

The moos turned to boos over the depiction of a popular new video game cow character.

People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) is protesting the design of Cow, a scooter-riding farm animal in the new [“Mario Kart World”](https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/mario-kart-world-switch-2/?srsltid=AfmBOoqVlnN7ArRSV0P3qWY0Ns1On6RpJLBGA-Fzh7mg1y5oOjDkAd9M) because the character wears a nose ring.

“Nose rings are used by the meat and dairy industries to exploit, control, and even drag animals to their deaths,” PETA said in a letter (in full below) Thursday to Nintendo President Shuntaro Furukawa.

Nintendo of America is headquartered in Redmond, Wash.

The game launched exclusively on the new Nintendo Switch 2 game console, which [released in June](https://www.geekwire.com/2025/nintendos-switch-2-arrives-with-long-lines-in-seattle-and-beyond-for-new-video-game-console/) to much fanfare. And Cow has become a breakout star, as [The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/07/13/arts/mario-kart-world-cow.html) reported in July, with videos on social media showcasing the bovine’s popularity.

PETA is less enthralled — at least when it comes to the nose ring. The organization is calling for Nintendo to redesign Cow’s look, so it can “race freely — without any painful reminders of the industries that treat animals like profit-making machines.”

Read PETA’s letter to Nintendo, and watch a trailer for “Mario Kart World” below:

> Dear Mr. Furukawa:
> 
> Greetings! I’m writing on behalf of People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA). PETA entities have more than 10 million members and supporters globally. We _herd_ there’s a new star in Mario Kart World: Cow! She is already winning hearts everywhere—including ours. But one detail has us hitting the brakes: The brass ring in Cow’s nose. Would you please show empathy towards bovines and remove the nose ring? Here’s why this is so important:
> 
> Nose rings are used by the meat and dairy industries to exploit, control, and even drag animals to their deaths. These brass rings are crudely stabbed through the sensitive septum of cows and bulls, which can cause lasting pain and discomfort. The dairy industry will also clip spiked nose rings on baby cows so that the comforting act of nursing from their mother causes her pain and the baby is rejected and kicked away. To control bulls, a chain might be fastened from the nose ring to the bull’s horn for even more pain-driven control.
> 
> The brass ring in Cow’s nose glosses over real world violence and cruelty to animals. That’s why we’re asking you to give this beloved bovine a small but meaningful upgrade: Remove the nose ring and let Cow race freely—without any painful reminders of the industries that treat animals like profit-making machines.
> 
> Every animal is some_one_. So leave the rings to Sonic and let Cow breathe free!

07/16/24[Learn more](https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/mario-kart-8-deluxe-switch/)

Meet some udderly adorable residents in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe!
============================================================

Take a drive down the winding paths of Moo Moo Meadows. Nestled in serene grasslands and dotted with spinning windmills, this course has been fittingly named for its legend-dairy moo moos.

To show our appreciation for these moojestic animals, we’ve gathered a few fun facts about the course.

![Image 15](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2024/meet-some-udderly-adorable-residents-in-mario-kart-8-deluxe/DejaMoo)

**Déjà moo!**
-------------

This course first appeared in the Mario Kart™ Wii game.

![Image 16](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2024/meet-some-udderly-adorable-residents-in-mario-kart-8-deluxe/SteerClear)

**Steer clear!**
----------------

There are groups of cows wandering the course. They look happy, don’t they? Try to avoid them… mostly because your kart doesn’t stand a chance against these stock-y citizens.

![Image 17](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2024/meet-some-udderly-adorable-residents-in-mario-kart-8-deluxe/Mole)

**A mole other obstacle!**
--------------------------

Moo moos aren’t the only creatures to avoid. Monty Mole can slow you down with raised dirt trails and by popping up from holes.

![Image 18](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2024/meet-some-udderly-adorable-residents-in-mario-kart-8-deluxe/SignOfTheTimes)

**Sign of the times!**
----------------------

You may see in-game sponsor banners around the course, like 1-Up Fuel and Green Service.

If you’d like to purchase the game, please click on the link below. And if you’re looking for even more revved up excitement, check out the [Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass\*](https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/mario-kart-8-deluxe-booster-course-pass-70070000013723-switch/)!

This paid DLC adds eight characters, 48 courses, and 16 Mii racing suits to the game. And racers who have an active [Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack](https://www.nintendo.com/us/switch/online/nintendo-switch-online/expansion-pack/) membership\*\* will have access to all of the DLC at no additional cost!
